table.name: Documents
table.purpose: Master list of documents (articles, CVs, reviews, etc.), each linked to a layout template and containing paragraphs stored in the Paragraphs table.

Document_ID.name: Document_ID
Document_ID.description: Primary key identifying each document. Referenced by Paragraphs.Document_ID, which stores the document's text content.

Document_Name.name: Document_Name
Document_Name.description: Human-readable title of the document (e.g. 'A history of Arts', 'Robbin CV', 'Customer reviews'). Unique per row.

Template_ID.name: Template_ID
Template_ID.description: Foreign key to Templates.Template_ID, selecting the template/layout used by the document. The lookup table's Template_Details labels are empty, so template meanings cannot be determined.

table.name: Paragraphs
table.purpose: Stores individual paragraphs extracted from documents; each row is one paragraph belonging to a document. In this sample the paragraph text values are country names, suggesting the documents are lists or texts about countries. The table likely also relates to Templates/Ref_Template_Types (paragraphs may be template-driven), though no direct join evidence exists for that.

Document_ID.name: Document_ID
Document_ID.description: Identifier of the document this paragraph belongs to; references Documents.Document_ID (many paragraphs per document).

Paragraph_ID.name: Paragraph_ID
Paragraph_ID.description: Primary key; unique identifier of the paragraph.

Paragraph_Text.name: Paragraph_Text
Paragraph_Text.description: Text content of the paragraph. In this data all values are country names (e.g. Somalia, Japan, Korea), so paragraphs here appear to be single country entries within country-list documents.

table.name: Ref_Template_Types
table.purpose: Lookup/reference table of template type categories. Each row is a distinct document template type (code + description) referenced by the Templates table.

Template_Type_Code.name: Template_Type_Code
Template_Type_Code.description: Short code identifying a template type (primary key). Values: AD=Advertisement, BK=Book, CV=CV, PP=Paper, PPT=Presentation. Referenced by Templates.Template_Type_Code.

Template_Type_Description.name: Template_Type_Description
Template_Type_Description.description: Human-readable label of the template type (e.g., Advertisement, Book, CV, Paper, Presentation).

table.name: Templates
table.purpose: A catalog of document templates, each with a type (presentation, CV, advertisement, paper, book), a version number, and an effective validity period. Templates are referenced by Documents, which presumably instantiate them. Note: the effective-from/to dates are inconsistent (From often later than To), suggesting the date data is synthetic or corrupted, so the temporal semantics are only tentative.

Date_Effective_From.name: effective_from_date
Date_Effective_From.description: Start of the template's validity/effective period, stored as a string. In many rows it is later than Date_Effective_To, so the data appears synthetic or corrupted; the intended meaning (validity start) is plausible but not confirmed by the values.

Date_Effective_To.name: effective_to_date
Date_Effective_To.description: End of the template's validity/effective period, stored as a string. Frequently earlier than the From date, undermining the validity-interval reading; treated as the nominal end date only.

Template_ID.name: template_id
Template_ID.description: Primary key uniquely identifying each template; referenced by Documents.Template_ID.

Template_Type_Code.name: template_type_code
Template_Type_Code.description: Code classifying the template's type, foreign key to Ref_Template_Types (PPT=Presentation, CV=CV, AD=Advertisement, PP=Paper, BK=Book).

Version_Number.name: version_number
Version_Number.description: Version of the template, integer 0-9, reused across templates (not unique). Marks different revisions of a template; exact semantics (e.g., whether 0 is a draft) are not evidenced.
